# R375 — actual phase grow/fill/publish overhead from model v2

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/spec investigation; the only artifact written is this report. Main's phase model lifetime v3 run remained under Main's ownership. No GPU/model/test/build/import/AST/profiler/service/process/Git/cleanup action was performed. No source, test, configuration, runtime environment, or existing receipt was changed.

## Finding

The closed actual-model v2 prompt transition reports `grow_fill_publish_ms=3364.974` and 3,370.024 ms for its enclosing successful-prompt callback. Its operation counters identify 768 checked payload writes, 768 checked readbacks, 768 byte comparisons, and 48 physical extent maps. The host call that submits each payload `gpu::copy` synchronously waits for its event and checks asynchronous errors. Therefore, the strongest low-risk performance candidate is reducing per-slot checked-copy round trips by batching bounded groups per layer while preserving explicit completion and every source/readback equality check. A small registered readback buffer is a separate second candidate because the present verification buffer is `std::vector<uint8_t>` (ordinary host allocation). A third cost, presently outside the operation timers, is the per-slot FNV-1a walk over every source byte and its diagnostic line; it may account for a meaningful part of the 1,406.742 ms timer gap, but no dedicated measurement identifies its share.

These times came from a `STRATA_TRACE=1`, validation/debug lifetime run. They locate work and call overhead; they are not accepted throughput or speedup evidence. Counter `host_elapsed_ms` values are nested and are not additive estimates of independent wall time. No proposed candidate is qualified by this audit.

## Actual v2 evidence and arithmetic

Read-only receipt: `/home/yayoi/.local/state/strata-sycl/post-reboot-tuning-20261007/main-phase-cache-model-lifetime-root-v2/record.json`, `commands/engine-phase-lifetime.stderr`, and `commands/engine-phase-lifetime.stdout`. Receipt is `active=false`, `passed=false`, `complete=false`; the engine command ended with `-15` after the harness mishandled the engine's valid early EOS. This investigation uses the completed `successful_prompt` evidence before that later lifecycle failure and does not reinterpret the receipt as a passed lifetime.

The exact `stage=successful_prompt` rows in `engine-phase-lifetime.stderr` are:

| Operation | Calls | Attempt / success bytes | Host elapsed ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| quiesce | 1 | 0 / 0 | 0.026 |
| physical allocation | 48 | 1,631,584,256 / 1,631,584,256 | 1.051 |
| map | 48 | 1,631,584,256 / 1,631,584,256 | 21.574 |
| H2D payload | 768 | 1,571,635,200 / 1,571,635,200 | 1,441.241 |
| D2H payload readback | 768 | 1,571,635,200 / 1,571,635,200 | 412.846 |
| payload compare | 768 | 1,571,635,200 / 1,571,635,200 | 78.016 |
| residency H2D | 1 | 98,304 / 98,304 | 1.519 |
| residency D2H | 1 | 98,304 / 98,304 | 0.151 |
| residency compare | 1 | 98,304 / 98,304 | 0.003 |
| publish | 1 | 0 / 0 | 1.757 |
| drain | 2 | 0 / 0 | 0.048 |
| unmap / invalidate / close / destroy / reserve / release | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0.000 |

The phase operation rows sum to 1,958.232 ms; subtracting that arithmetic subtotal from 3,364.974 ms leaves 1,406.742 ms. This is an accounting gap, not a separately measured stage: the enclosing timer includes source lookup, per-slot logging/hash, loop/control work and runtime/measurement overhead that these operation rows do not time. The physical/map rows each describe 48 layer extents, not 768 slot-level mappings. Each of the 768 payload directions moved 1,571,635,200 logical source bytes (2,046,400 bytes/slot averaged across layers); those equal byte totals show application-requested copy sizes, not measured PCIe/DRAM transactions. The map/physical total is the larger, granularity-rounded extent allocation size. Residency transfer was a separate 98,304-byte complete 48-layer-by-512-expert int32 table in each direction.

The enclosing callback is 3,370.024 ms, while `grow_fill_publish_ms` is 3,364.974 ms. The additional 5.050 ms belongs to surrounding successful-prompt work. Do not add the nested `cycle`/`successful_prompt` rows to either value. The receipt reports 912/912 mapped slots, 1,927,282,688 mapped/retained physical bytes, and free memory increasing from 1,838,514,176 to 4,162,195,456 bytes after prompt retirement and growth. These are capacity/lifetime observations, not evidence that the cache transfer used that much PCIe bandwidth.

## Source path and likely targets

At the supplied base revision `54385d6f975a13df5da87f489614d0b729d2aba6`, `generate.cpp` maps the 48 extra extents, then visits ranks 3–18 for each of 48 layers and calls `phase_fill` once per expert before one checked publish. In `PhaseCacheOwner::fill_checked`, each call invokes backend write, then backend read into `verification_`, then `memcmp`; it only marks the slot filled/staged after all three succeed. `GpuBackend::write/read` route through `gpu::copy`; `gpu::copy` calls `queue.memcpy` and `Runtime::wait(event)`, whose implementation calls `event.wait_and_throw()` and `check_async()`. Thus the two 768-count copy operations are per-slot blocking submission/completion boundaries in this implementation. The 48 map calls correspond to one extra extent per layer; base mapping, reservation, and unmapping are outside this successful-prompt transition.

`ExpertCache::phase_fill` additionally hashes all `bytes` of the immutable source with FNV-1a and emits a `slot_checked` line after `fill_checked` returns. The 768 calls therefore cause a further CPU traversal of 1,571,635,200 source bytes after `memcmp`, plus 768 formatted diagnostics. This work is outside `h2d`, `d2h`, and `compare` timers. The current source checks exact byte equality, and the hash is supplementary evidence; any implementation that changes hash timing or calculation must keep the required per-slot correctness evidence and must not replace the checked comparison with a hash-only condition.

### Candidate order

1. **Bounded per-layer batch, targeting 48 groups of 16 extras.** Add a batch owner API which stages at most one layer's 16 immutable Host-USM blobs, submits a bounded H2D batch, waits for and checks completion, performs bounded readback(s), compares every exact payload byte against its corresponding immutable source, and only then marks all 16 slots filled/staged. The actual extra-slot records contain exactly 16 payloads per layer; the largest group is layer 47 at 42,598,400 bytes (16 × 2,662,400), and all 48 extra groups total the measured 1,571,635,200 bytes. An ideal first shape is one contiguous 256-byte-stride-padded layer transfer in each direction and one completion boundary per direction per layer. The blobs are individually sized and slot strides are 256-byte rounded, so the staging layout, padding bytes, and readback comparison bounds must be explicit; do not overread source blobs or make slot padding visible as a payload. Bound storage to one layer and preserve it until its commands complete. The call reduction target is 768 to 48 per direction, but physical byte traffic may remain similar and host packing adds CPU work; no speedup follows from call counts alone.
2. **Registered, bounded readback destination.** `PhaseCacheOwner::verification_` is currently a reusable vector sized to the largest blob. A host-USM or supported registered host buffer of that same bound may avoid repeated pageable-destination staging for D2H. Keep one buffer alive until checked completion and compare on the CPU only after completion; test under exact SourceLLVM/UR/Level Zero provider and device. This is not a replacement for byte comparisons, checked completion, or fail-stop error handling. Registration/host-USM might have no benefit or increase cost on a particular runtime; measure before selecting it.
3. **Account for/stream the supplemental hash.** The 1.57 GB FNV pass and per-slot diagnostics are uninstrumented inside each `phase_fill` call. Preserve the current independent exact comparison and full hash evidence in the initial candidate. A later source-only design can determine whether FNV can be computed during a single exact compare pass without weakening failure behavior; a custom scalar compare loop may lose optimized `memcmp` throughput, so benchmark both. Do not infer the hash's time from the 1,406.742 ms residual.
4. **Leave extent map and residency publication lower priority for this transition.** Map+physical time is 22.625 ms; table upload+readback+compare+publish is 3.430 ms, versus the 1,441.241 ms H2D counter and 412.846 ms D2H counter. Keep the complete residency-table upload/readback/compare and one checked publish. No evidence supports optimizing map geometry or deleting the one final publish first.

### Acceptance conditions for any follow-up

Use a fresh serialized real-model comparison only after the current lifetime run is closed. Preserve all selected layer/expert IDs and slot offsets; compare exact source and destination payload bytes for every admitted expert; preserve all host/device residency entries and checked upload/readback equality before readers become ready. Every submitted write/read must have a checked completion boundary before its source, packed buffer, readback buffer, physical extent or owner can be reused or released. On unknown completion or any mismatch/error, poison/fail-stop and retain uncertain owners; do not publish partial rows, retry, free in-flight USM, or relax validation. Keep reader invalidation, graph/session reader retirement, and checked drain ordering for later detach/close. Add fail-stop coverage for failures at every batch submission, completion, readback, compare and publication boundary before runtime qualification. Performance evidence must come from the unchanged upstream benchmark protocol, not this trace-enabled lifetime diagnostic.

The immutable expert weights are already owned by a 50.29 GB Host-USM arena and `ArenaExpertSource::phase_blob` returns a range-checked pointer into that owner. The phase VMM cache's static expert payloads can therefore be reconstructed from host memory after checked invalidation/reader retirement/detach and a later checked refill; VRAM copy is a cache lease, not the sole copy of those static weights. Persistent GDN recurrent state and KV/session state are different live model state: this cache audit does not establish them as reconstructible from the expert arena, and they must remain owned and numerically unchanged across any refill optimization. No candidate here resets, drops, or recreates those states.

## SYCL/Level Zero evidence and limits

The installed local path inspected is the SourceLLVM v7.1.1 / SYCL / Unified Runtime Level Zero backend cited in the existing R360/R362/R372 reports; actual v2 runtime identified one Arc B570, one context device, Level Zero backend id 2, and reported 64 KiB device-recommended/device-minimum/context-minimum granularity. SYCL's USM table defines host allocations as host-resident and accessible to devices. `sycl::malloc_host` is already used by `PinnedArena` to create host-USM expert blocks. The current per-call payload source is therefore already owned Host-USM; replacing it with another pinning step is not a promising first target. The readback destination is ordinary `std::vector<uint8_t>`, so registered/host-USM readback is the distinct question.

Primary references:

- Khronos [SYCL 2020 specification, USM allocation characteristics](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html): host USM is host-located and accessible by host and devices; this is an accessibility guarantee, not a transfer-speed guarantee.
- Level Zero [zeMemAllocHost](https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/api/apis/mem.html#zememallochost): host allocations are accessible by host and context devices and are “frequently used as staging areas to transfer data to or from devices.” This does not guarantee that a particular readback will be faster than the current vector path.
- Khronos [SYCL host/device interaction](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/interaction-with-host-code.html): host interaction and concurrent access remain subject to the relevant execution completion and USM capability rules; this proposal relies on checked event completion before CPU validation.
- Intel [oneAPI DPC++ multi-tile memory guide](https://intel.github.io/llvm/MultiTileCardWithLevelZero.html): `malloc_host` provides host USM for the context device(s); it does not establish a device-specific throughput result for this application.
- Existing local primary-source audits: `research-phase-vmm-real-api-lifetime-round360-v1.txt` and `research-vmm-map-failure-atomicity-round362-v1.txt` cover VMM geometry and unknown-map fail-stop; `research-phase-all-expert-cache-lease-round367-v1.txt` covers full static-resident invalidation/remap lifetime; `research-phase-stock-supervisor-admission-round372-v2.txt` corrects stock lifecycle admission; `research-decode-route-reuse-instrumentation-round370-v2.txt` is unrelated route-capture work and is not repeated here.

No external project performance claim is transferred to Strata. Candidate batch sizes, staging-memory cost, pageable-vs-registered readback timing, GPU-copy overlap, and all throughput effects are unmeasured. `requested_native_dequant_batch=1` is an engine-path configuration line, not evidence that phase refill itself is batched.
